ppl.text: The history of computing spans the development of machines that perform calculations automatically. Early devices such as the abacus and the slide rule aided arithmetic long before electronic computers existed. The modern era of computing began in the twentieth century with electromechanical and electronic machines. Over successive decades, computing hardware grew faster and smaller, while software became more abstract and portable. These advances transformed science, industry, and daily life in ways that continue to unfold.
